## 3. Prize-pool audit: the core finding

Method: for each of the 786 bodies, check (a) is the category named in `## Prize Categories`, and (b) is there **substantive use**: code-level evidence (SDK import, endpoint, env var, CLI) or ≥3 substantive mentions. "Declared+substantive" is the real pool. Script: `audit.py` → `prize-audit.json`.

| Category | Prize | Declared | **Declared + substantive** | Strongest competitor | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Entire** | $100 | 22 | **1** | 0♥, a single "first checkpoint" line | 🟢 **Wide open** |
| **Arduino** | $200 | 3 | **1** | 0♥ | 🟢 Open, *but needs an UNO Q board* |
| **DigitalOcean** | $200 | 10 | **4** | BMW manual (32♥, DO Serverless Inference → Gemma) | 🟢 Thin. Nobody self-hosts an open model on a Droplet. |
| **Temporal** | $100 | 13 | **6** | Suniye (28♥, wins once max) | 🟢 Thin |
| **Tiger Data** | $100 | 6 | **6** | — | 🟢 Thin |
| **Mastra** | $100 | 11 | **7** | Suniye | 🟢 Thin (TS-only) |
| **Tinker** | $200 | 16 | **9** | **Kharcha (30♥, 97% vs 28% baseline, adapter exported)** | 🟡 Thin, with one excellent entry |
| SerpApi | $100 | 12 | 12 | Bus Guardian (35♥) | 🟡 |
| Sentry Agent Tracing | $100 | 21 | 15 | SafePlate (33♥), Suniye | 🟡 |
| Backboard | $100 | 22 | 15 | Kharcha | 🟡 |
| **TabPFN** | $200 | 24 | **21** | Bus Guardian (35♥); most others 0–5♥ | 🟡 Moderate. The quality bar is low. |
| MongoDB Atlas | $100 | 41 | 23 | — | 🟠 |
| GitHub Copilot | $100 | 35 | 31 | — | 🟠 |
| ElevenLabs | $100 | 61 | 45 | — | 🔴 |
| Render | $200 | 129 | **113** | Kharcha, many | 🔴 Saturated |
| Gemma | $200 | 279 | **265** | Vim trainer (40♥) | 🔴 **Saturated (34% of field)** |

### Reading the pools
1. **Featured $200 pools: Gemma (265) and Render (113) are where people crowded in. DigitalOcean (4) and Tinker (9) were skipped.** Same prize money, a 30–60× difference in competition. This is the Dog Days/Generosity pattern again: *entrants pile into whatever they can call from an SDK in ten minutes, and avoid anything that needs an account, credits or a training run.*
2. **The one-win cap frees up slots.** Suniye declares 11 categories and Kharcha declares 3. Each can take only **one** slot. A strong multi-category entrant makes the *other* pools they're in weaker than the raw count suggests.
3. **Entire is basically uncontested.** 22 entries name it, and 1 shows any substance (one sentence about a first checkpoint). Recording agent sessions costs nothing when you build with Claude Code anyway.
4. **Nobody serves a *fine-tuned* open model from a box they control.** Kharcha serves its adapter through Tinker's sampling API on Render. The BMW entry calls DO's managed serverless inference. "My weights, my Droplet" is unclaimed, and it is the strongest possible answer to the mandatory *"Why Does Open Innovation Matter?"* section.

## 4. Pattern saturation (what NOT to build)

- **"4B SFT extraction model + eval table" is taken 4×** (Kharcha, DawaaiDost (text near-identical to Kharcha), OneInbox, Aaji's Pill Clerk). Kharcha set the bar: 150 held-out, all-fields 28% → 97%, beats gpt-oss-120b zero-shot, adapter exported. **A Tinker entry has to be measured on a different axis to stand out.**
- The prompt's own example list is saturated: allergy meal planners (SafePlate, AllergenPal, PlateMate, Roomiee Bites…), study buddies (≥15), voice memo → recipe books (Heirloom, Nani's Recipe Book, Salt & Story…), medicine reminders for grandparents (≥6).
- Local-Gemma journaling/companion apps: dozens.
- **Untouched:** migraine/headache (0 titles), chronic-flare forecasting, any "the friend's own notes → forecast" pipeline that pairs a fine-tuned parser with TabPFN.

## 5. Verified capability notes (primary sources)

| Claim | Status | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tinker fine-tunes **Qwen3.5-4B** (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, $0.737/M train tokens), Qwen3-8B, gpt-oss, Nemotron, Kimi, etc. **No Gemma.** | ✅ | [Tinker Models & Pricing](https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/models/models_and_pricing/index.md) |
| Tinker LoRA weights are downloadable and can be merged into a HF model / PEFT adapter | ✅ (cookbook: *Merge into a HuggingFace Model*, *Build a PEFT LoRA Adapter*; Kharcha shows a 146 MB adapter downloaded) | [Tinker docs index](https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/llms.txt) |
| Tinker exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for any sampler checkpoint (beta, low traffic) | ✅ | [OpenAI-compatible API](https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/compatible-apis/openai/index.md) |
| TabPFN-3.5 base runs **locally** via the `tabpfn` package (open weights, TABPFN-3-5 License v1.0, code Apache-2.0). Plus/Thinking are API-only. | ✅ | [TabPFN Models](https://docs.priorlabs.ai/models.md) |
| TabPFN takes raw pandas DataFrames: no encoding, imputation or scaling. Shapley explanations via `tabpfn-extensions[interpretability]` | ✅ | [Quickstart](https://docs.priorlabs.ai/quickstart.md), [Interpretability](https://docs.priorlabs.ai/capabilities/interpretability.md) |
| Entire captures Claude Code sessions as git-linked checkpoints: `entire enable -y --agent claude-code`, `entire checkpoint list` | ✅ | [Entire Quickstart](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart.md) |
| Sentry Agent Tracing supports Python and Mastra. Python `OpenAIIntegration(include_prompts=False)` + conversation IDs; view at Explore → Agents | ✅ | [Sentry Set Up Agents](https://docs.sentry.io/product/agents/getting-started/) |

## 6. What historically wins (one paragraph)

Writing quality is **explicitly weighted most heavily** here. That's new versus earlier Weekend Challenges, and it rewards exactly what the strongest current entries do: a named person, a measured result, and an honest caveat. The BMW entry's "He said / What changed" feedback table and Kharcha's results table with "Two honest caveats" are the two best-written posts in the field. Prior DEV patterns still hold: a live demo plus a repo plus a video, a personal opening, a specific number, OSI license, and the un-marketed capability as the differentiator. On the category criterion, the test is **"does the project collapse without it?"**, not "is it present?".

# 02 — Winning Ideas + The Stack

**Constraint that drives everything: T-12h at writing time.** Every idea below is scoped to ship in about 9 build hours plus 2 writing hours, using Claude Code.

## The stack decision (the actual question)

You win **once** per challenge, but every category you *genuinely* use is an independent pool. So we pick categories by **expected value = (1 / real pool size) × how structurally necessary the tech is to the project**. We do **not** pick by "can I mention it". An unjustified category isn't free: it adds code, eats hours, and spreads the post thin, and writing quality is the most heavily weighted criterion.

### ✅ IN: the core five (each is load-bearing)

| # | Category | Prize | Real pool | Role in the project (why it can't be removed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Tinker** | $200 | 9 | Fine-tunes the small open model that turns your friend's messy notes into data. Without it the base 4B mis-parses their shorthand, and every forecast built on those rows is wrong. |
| 2 | **TabPFN** | $200 | 21 | The forecaster. Your friend has ~60–120 days of history. That's far too small to train a model, and it's exactly what a tabular foundation model does in-context. Local `tabpfn`, so health data never leaves the box. |
| 3 | **DigitalOcean** | $200 | 4 | One Droplet runs **everything**: the merged fine-tuned GGUF, TabPFN on CPU, and the app. No third-party inference at runtime. "My weights, my box" is the open-innovation thesis. |
| 4 | **Entire** | $100 | **1** | Records every Claude Code session as git-linked checkpoints. The post links the checkpoint behind each key decision. Effectively uncontested. |
| 5 | **Sentry Agent Tracing** | $100 | 15 | Traces the parse → forecast → explain agent. The **base-vs-tuned latency/token traces double as the Tinker proof.** |

### 🟡 STRETCH: only if you're ahead at the Hour-6 checkpoint

| # | Category | Prize | Pool | Genuine role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | **Temporal** | $100 | 6 | The 8 AM "morning check" (parse yesterday → forecast → notify) as a durable workflow with retries. A cron would do the job, but durability is the honest pitch: a heads-up that silently fails is worse than none. |
| 7 | **GitHub Copilot** | $100 | 31 | GitHub Action that re-runs the parser eval on every push and fails if the tuned model drops below baseline. Copilot reviews the PR. |

### ❌ OUT: deliberately skipped (say so in the post, briefly)

| Category | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Gemma** ($200) | 265 competitors (34% of the field), and Tinker can't fine-tune Gemma. Bolting it on as a second model is the "useless overflow" you asked to avoid. |
| **Render** ($200) | 113 competitors, and DigitalOcean is already the host. Two hosts is overflow. |
| ElevenLabs | 45 competitors. Sending health voice notes to a cloud API **contradicts the privacy thesis** in the open-innovation section. |
| MongoDB / Tiger Data | SQLite on the Droplet *is* the privacy story. A managed DB adds a third party holding health rows. |
| Mastra | TypeScript. Splitting a Python ML stack in two costs hours you don't have. *(See Idea 4 if you're a TS person.)* |
| Backboard / SerpApi | Cloud memory or web search add nothing to a personal forecast. |
| Arduino | Needs an **Arduino UNO Q**. **If you own one, it's a 1-competitor $200 pool. Tell me and I'll re-plan around it.** |

**Net: 5 categories genuinely entered (3 × $200 featured + 2 × $100), plus 2 stretch.** All 5 core categories have ≤21 real competitors. Three have ≤4.

---

## Ranked ideas

Scores are 1–5 per criterion. W = Writing (×2, weighted most), R = Relevance, C = Creativity, T = Technical, P = Partner-tech, F = feasible in ~9h.

| Rank | Idea | W×2 | R | C | T | P | F | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Heads Up: a migraine early-warning built for one friend** | 10 | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | **33** |
| 2 | Same pipeline, different friend (flare/sleep/training/café sales) | 9 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 31 |
| 3 | "Their taste, in the weights": Tinker DPO on the friend's own A/B picks | 9 | 5 | 5 | 3 | 4 | 2 | 28 |
| 4 | TS thin-pool sweep: Mastra + Temporal + Tiger Data + Sentry + Entire + DO | 7 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 3 | 26 |
| 5 | Arduino UNO Q physical agent *(only if you own the board)* | 8 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 5 | 2 | 27 |

### 1. Heads Up: a migraine early-warning built for one friend ⭐ RECOMMENDED

**Who:** one real friend who gets migraines. (No friend with migraines? Use Idea 2. The pipeline is identical; only the nouns change.)

**What:** they text their day the way they already would: *"slept 5h, 3 coffees, stared at excel till 9, bit of a neck thing"*. A **Qwen3.5-4B fine-tuned on Tinker** parses it into a row (sleep, caffeine, screen hours, stress, meals skipped, neck/aura flags). A free weather API adds barometric pressure change. **TabPFN**, running locally, reads their whole history in-context and returns *"68% chance of a migraine tomorrow"*, plus the **Shapley "why"**: *"mostly: 5h sleep + pressure dropping 9 hPa"*. Everything runs on **one DigitalOcean Droplet**, so no model provider ever sees their health notes.

**Why it wins:**
- *Writing:* a real person, a real body, a real "she said" moment. Health-for-a-friend reads as the most emotionally honest form of the theme, and **zero** of 786 entries cover migraines.
- *Open innovation (mandatory section):* the three strongest answers the prompt itself suggests, all genuinely true at once. *Keeps data off a server they don't control* (Droplet). *Lets you fine-tune* (Tinker → downloadable weights). *Costs ~nothing to run* (one small Droplet, no per-call fees).
- *Tinker on a new axis:* Kharcha owns "SFT accuracy table". We add two axes nobody has: **(a) accuracy on the friend's *real* handwritten notes (human-labelled), and (b) the downstream effect, meaning how much the base model's parse errors distort the forecast versus the tuned model's.** Plus CPU latency on the actual $ Droplet.
- *TabPFN:* the textbook fit. Tiny table, no training, and Shapley explanations make the forecast *trustworthy to a non-technical friend*. Most of the 21 TabPFN entries just call `.predict`.

**First-scene hook (draft):**
> *Priya gets about four migraines a month. She can feel two of them coming. The other two arrive at 3 PM in the middle of something she can't leave. I can't fix her head. But I had a weekend, a 4-billion-parameter model, and 74 days of her texting me "ugh, head" — so I built her a weather forecast for migraines.*

**Hour budget:** about 9h build + 2h write (detail in `03-PLAYBOOK-heads-up.md`).
**Deployment:** DO Droplet (Basic, 4 vCPU / 8 GB, ~$48/mo prorated ≈ $1.60/day; destroy after judging). Live demo URL with a **demo profile** (synthetic data). The friend's real profile is private, behind a passphrase.
**Honest weaknesses:** (1) ~60–120 labelled days is a small sample, so forecasts will be modestly accurate. Report cross-validated AUC with its uncertainty and frame it as a "heads-up, not a diagnosis". (2) It depends on the friend supplying history *tonight*. (3) GGUF conversion of Qwen3.5 is the riskiest technical step. The fallback is serving the adapter via Tinker's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with the Droplet still hosting the app and TabPFN.

### 2. Same pipeline, different friend
Swap the nouns and keep the stack: eczema/asthma/IBS flare forecast; a runner friend's "niggle → injury" log; a café-owner friend's WhatsApp orders → tomorrow's bake quantities (note: "Crumb AI" café forecaster exists, 0♥). Slightly lower creativity because these are closer to existing entries.

### 3. "Their taste, in the weights"
The friend picks A/B between two drafts (messages, captions, cover letters) for 30 minutes. Tinker DPO on their picks, then a blind win-rate versus base. This is the most on-theme use of fine-tuning there is (*a model trained by one person, for one person*). But it depends on ~100 preference pairs from the friend tonight, and DPO tuning is riskier in 9h. **Only pick this if the friend is sitting next to you.**

### 4. TS thin-pool sweep
For a TypeScript builder: Mastra agent over an open model (Ollama on a DO Droplet) + Temporal durability + Tiger Data pgvector memory + Sentry (has a Mastra guide) + Entire. That's six pools of ≤15. Weaker on writing because the stack drives the story rather than the friend, and Suniye already plays this exact hand (11 categories, 28♥).

### 5. Arduino UNO Q
The pool has 1 real entry. If you physically own a UNO Q, a sensing/acting agent for a friend (pill-box lid sensor, plant, door) is the highest-EV $200 in the contest. Without the board it's impossible.

## Recommendation
**Build Idea 1 with the core-five stack.** Add Temporal only if the Droplet is serving by Hour 6. Publish by **05:30 UTC**, 90 minutes before the 06:59 UTC deadline.

# Vibecoding Bootstrap — Hour 0 of EVERY hackathon build

> The standard scaffolding the coding agent must set up **before writing any feature code**. Goal: an automated, low-token, self-documenting vibecoding loop. **Every build playbook references this as its first build step.** Keep it lightweight — this is a hackathon, not production; simple hygiene only, no deep security.

---

## What gets created first (in order)

1. **`memory.md`** — the project's running brain (read first, updated last, every task).
2. **`AGENTS.md`** — the agent contract (how to work in this repo).
3. **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`** — same rules, for Copilot specifically (can be a one-line pointer to AGENTS.md).
4. **`README.md`** — what it is + how to run (stub now, grows as you build).
5. **`.env.example`** + **`.gitignore`** — never commit real secrets; `.env` is git-ignored.
6. **`scripts/`** (optional) — `setup.sh` / `run.sh` so the demo is reproducible in one command.
7. **`git init`** + first commit — Conventional Commits from the start.

## The memory.md protocol (the core of the automated loop)

`memory.md` is the single source of truth that keeps each prompt cheap and stateful.

**Rule for every prompt/task:**
1. **Read `memory.md` first** for context — do NOT re-scan the whole repo.
2. Do the task.
3. **Update `memory.md` last:** append what changed, decisions made, and next step. **Summarize aggressively** — bullet points, not transcripts. Prune stale detail. Keep it short to minimize token use next time.

Starter `memory.md`:

```markdown
# memory.md — <project> brain
> Read this first every task. Update it last. Keep it terse to save tokens.

## What this is
<one line>

## Stack
<languages/frameworks/services>

## Status snapshot
- Phase: <x>
- Last task: <what just shipped>
- Next: <immediate next step>

## Key decisions (why)
- <decision> — <reason>

## Open questions / TODO
- <item>

## File map (only what matters)
- `path` — purpose
```

## AGENTS.md (the contract the coding agent follows)

Keep it short. Include:

- **Loop rule:** "Read `memory.md` before each task; update it after. Summarize; don't dump."
- **Context discipline:** edit only relevant files; don't ingest the whole repo; prefer summaries.
- **Design rule:** "For any web UI, use the `frontend-design` skill." (See skills note below.)
- **Commits:** "After each working increment, commit with Conventional Commits." (format below)
- **Run discipline:** keep `README.md` run steps current; secrets only in `.env` (git-ignored).
- **Stop conditions:** ask before large refactors or adding heavy dependencies.

`.github/copilot-instructions.md` can simply say: *"Follow `AGENTS.md` in the repo root. Read `memory.md` first; update it last; keep context tight."*

## Skills: will they auto-fire?

Yes — heuristically. Copilot CLI auto-discovers `SKILL.md` skills from `~/.copilot/skills/`, `.github/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` and invokes one when the request matches its `description`. So **`frontend-design` fires automatically when you ask to build/style web UI** — but it's model judgment, not a guaranteed hook on a "UI phase." To make it reliable, **state it in `AGENTS.md`** ("use frontend-design for web UI") and/or name it in the prompt during the UI step.

> For hackathons, let it run with full creative freedom (bold, distinctive). If the project has an existing design system, add: "use frontend-design but conform to existing design tokens."

## Conventional Commits (auto, lightweight)

Format: `<type>(optional-scope): short summary`. Types you'll actually use:

| type | when |
|---|---|
| `feat` | new feature / capability |
| `fix` | bug fix |
| `docs` | README/markdown |

# Heads Up: Full A-to-Z Winning Playbook

> Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend · deadline **2026-10-05 06:59 UTC** · target publish **05:30 UTC**
> Categories: **Tinker · TabPFN · DigitalOcean · Entire · Sentry Agent Tracing** (+ Temporal, Copilot stretch) · overall prize.

> **⚠️ The friend must be real.** The rules require "a real problem for a friend or loved one", and the post's power comes from a real reaction. Every `[BRACKET]` below gets filled with real data. **Never invent a metric, a quote, or a person.** If your friend doesn't get migraines, use the swap table in §1.5. The architecture stays identical.

## TABLE OF CONTENTS
I. Strategy · II. Build (hour-by-hour) · III. Persuasion · IV. Full draft post · V. Promotion · VI. Submission checklist

---

# PART I — STRATEGY & POSITIONING

## 1.1 The thesis (memorize this)
**"I can't fix [Friend]'s head, but I can give them a forecast. A tiny open model I fine-tuned reads their messy texts, a tabular foundation model reads their history, and it all runs on one box I control, so their health notes never touch anyone else's API."**

## 1.2 Judging criteria → design choices

| Criterion | Design choice that scores it |
|---|---|
| **Writing (weighted most)** | Real friend, real first scene, a results table with honest caveats, a "[Friend] said / what I changed" table (copy the BMW entry's best move), 6–9 min read. |
| Relevance (open AI at the core) | Two open models are the product: a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B (weights downloaded, self-hosted) + local TabPFN-3.5. Remove either and nothing works. |
| Creativity | Migraine forecasting: 0 of 786 entries. A "weather forecast for your head" framing. The Shapley "why" turns a probability into advice. |
| Technical execution | Live URL + repo + 90-second video. Eval scripts in the repo reproduce every number. Sentry traces prove it runs. |
| Partner tech | Each of the 5 is load-bearing (see §2.1). The post has one subsection per category with a screenshot or number. |

## 1.3 Persona (who reads it)
A DEV judge reading 900 entries in a week. They've seen 265 "local Gemma companion" posts. They reward: **a person, a number, a working link, honesty.** They punish: a stack list without a reason, invented stats, and dead demos.

## 1.4 Cut list (do NOT build)
- ❌ Accounts/auth. One passphrase-protected private profile + a public demo profile.
- ❌ Mobile app. A responsive web page they can "Add to Home Screen".
- ❌ Voice input. A cloud voice API contradicts the privacy thesis, and local Whisper costs an hour.
- ❌ Gemma, Render, ElevenLabs, a vector DB (see `02`).
- ❌ Push notifications (unless Temporal stretch). The page shows tomorrow's forecast. The friend checks it at night.

## 1.5 Friend swap table (same code, different nouns)

| Friend's situation | Notes they write | Row fields (Tinker parses) | TabPFN target |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Migraines (default)** | "5h sleep, 3 coffees, excel till 9, neck tight" | sleep_h, caffeine, screen_h, stress 1–5, skipped_meal, neck, aura, alcohol, cycle_day? | migraine_next_day (0/1) |

## 2.1 Stack (and each piece's job)

| Layer | Choice | Why this, not the alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Parser model | **Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA, trained on Tinker** (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B`, $0.737/M train tokens) | 4B Q4 fits in about 3 GB and runs on a CPU Droplet. The 9B is more accurate zero-shot but roughly 2× slower on CPU. The fine-tune closes that gap, and that's the Tinker proof. |
| Teacher (dataset labels only) | A large open model sampled on Tinker (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B` or `moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6`) | It's open too, so the whole pipeline is open weights end to end. Used **offline** on synthetic notes only, never on the friend's real notes. |
| Forecaster | **TabPFN-3.5, local `tabpfn` package** + `tabpfn-extensions[interpretability]` | Base TabPFN-3.5 runs locally, so health rows stay on the box. Plus/Thinking are API-only, and that's exactly why we don't use them. Raw DataFrame in, no encoding needed. |
| Serving | **llama.cpp → GGUF Q4_K_M via Ollama** on the Droplet (OpenAI-compatible `:11434/v1`) | The same OpenAI client works against Tinker (eval) and Ollama (prod), and Sentry's OpenAI integration traces both. |
| App | FastAPI + one HTML page (frontend-design skill) + SQLite | Smallest thing that works. SQLite lives on the Droplet: no third-party DB. |
| Host | **DigitalOcean Droplet** `s-4vcpu-8gb`, Ubuntu 24.04, Caddy + `<ip>.sslip.io` for HTTPS | Self-hosting the *fine-tuned* model is the unclaimed DO story. (Serverless Inference can't serve your own LoRA.) |
| Tracing | **Sentry** Python SDK + `OpenAIIntegration(include_prompts=False)` + manual agent/tool spans | `include_prompts=False` keeps health text out of Sentry: the same privacy line, applied to observability. |
| Build provenance | **Entire** (`entire enable -y --agent claude-code`) | Every Claude Code session becomes a checkpoint tied to a commit. Link 3–4 key ones in the post. |
| Weather | Open-Meteo historical + forecast API (free, no key) | Pressure change is a widely reported migraine trigger. It gives TabPFN a feature the friend doesn't have to log. |

## 2.3 Critical code skeletons
> These are skeletons. API names come from the docs pages cited in `01` §5. Lines marked `# verify` should be checked against the linked doc when you implement.

**Tinker SFT (`train/sft.py`)** (from the [quickstart](https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/quickstart/index.md)):
```python
import json, random, tinker
SYSTEM = "Extract a JSON row with keys: sleep_h, caffeine_cups, screen_h, stress, skipped_meal, alcohol_units, neck_tension, aura, exercise_min, notes_other. Output JSON only."
sc = tinker.ServiceClient()
tc = sc.create_lora_training_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", rank=32)
tok = tc.get_tokenizer()

def datum(note, row):
    prompt = tok.apply_chat_template([{"role":"system","content":SYSTEM},{"role":"user","content":note}],
                                     add_generation_prompt=True)          # verify: renderer for Qwen3.5 (disable thinking)
    completion = tok.encode(json.dumps(row) + tok.eos_token, add_special_tokens=False)
    full = prompt + completion
    return tinker.types.Datum(
        model_input=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(full[:-1]),         # verify field name: input vs model_input
        loss_fn_inputs={"target_tokens": full[1:],
                        "weights": [0.0]*(len(prompt)-1) + [1.0]*len(completion)})

data = [json.loads(l) for l in open("data/train.jsonl")]
for epoch in range(3):
    random.shuffle(data)
    for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
        batch = [datum(d["note"], d["row"]) for d in data[i:i+16]]
        fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, loss_fn="cross_entropy")
        tc.optim_step(tinker.types.AdamParams(learning_rate=2e-4)).result()
        print(epoch, i, fb.result().metrics)                               # log loss for the post's curve
path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name="heads-up-v1").result().path        # verify; -> tinker://... sampler path
print(path)
```

**Forecast + why (`app/forecast.py`):**
```python
import pandas as pd
from tabpfn import TabPFNClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import RepeatedStratifiedKFold, cross_val_score

def train_eval(hist: pd.DataFrame):
    X, y = hist.drop(columns=["date","migraine_next_day"]), hist["migraine_next_day"]
    cv = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=5, random_state=0)
    auc = cross_val_score(TabPFNClassifier(), X, y, cv=cv, scoring="roc_auc")
    return auc.mean(), auc.std()

def forecast(hist, today_row):
    clf = TabPFNClassifier().fit(hist.drop(columns=["date","migraine_next_day"]), hist["migraine_next_day"])
    p = clf.predict_proba(today_row)[0, 1]
    # Shapley drivers: tabpfn-extensions interpretability (shapiq) -> top-3 features by |value|  # verify API in docs
    return p
```

```python
import json, random, tinker
SYSTEM = "Extract a JSON row with keys: sleep_h, caffeine_cups, screen_h, stress, skipped_meal, alcohol_units, neck_tension, aura, exercise_min, notes_other. Output JSON only."
sc = tinker.ServiceClient()
tc = sc.create_lora_training_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", rank=32)
tok = tc.get_tokenizer()

def datum(note, row):
    prompt = tok.apply_chat_template([{"role":"system","content":SYSTEM},{"role":"user","content":note}],
                                     add_generation_prompt=True)          # verify: renderer for Qwen3.5 (disable thinking)
    completion = tok.encode(json.dumps(row) + tok.eos_token, add_special_tokens=False)
    full = prompt + completion
    return tinker.types.Datum(
        model_input=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(full[:-1]),         # verify field name: input vs model_input
        loss_fn_inputs={"target_tokens": full[1:],
                        "weights": [0.0]*(len(prompt)-1) + [1.0]*len(completion)})

data = [json.loads(l) for l in open("data/train.jsonl")]
for epoch in range(3):
    random.shuffle(data)
    for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
        batch = [datum(d["note"], d["row"]) for d in data[i:i+16]]
        fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, loss_fn="cross_entropy")
        tc.optim_step(tinker.types.AdamParams(learning_rate=2e-4)).result()
        print(epoch, i, fb.result().metrics)                               # log loss for the post's curve
path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name="heads-up-v1").result().path        # verify; -> tinker://... sampler path
print(path)
```

import pandas as pd
from tabpfn import TabPFNClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import RepeatedStratifiedKFold, cross_val_score

def train_eval(hist: pd.DataFrame):
    X, y = hist.drop(columns=["date","migraine_next_day"]), hist["migraine_next_day"]
    cv = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=5, random_state=0)
    auc = cross_val_score(TabPFNClassifier(), X, y, cv=cv, scoring="roc_auc")
    return auc.mean(), auc.std()

def forecast(hist, today_row):
    clf = TabPFNClassifier().fit(hist.drop(columns=["date","migraine_next_day"]), hist["migraine_next_day"])
    p = clf.predict_proba(today_row)[0, 1]
    # Shapley drivers: tabpfn-extensions interpretability (shapiq) -> top-3 features by |value|  # verify API in docs
    return p
```

import json, random, tinker
SYSTEM = "Extract a JSON row with keys: sleep_h, caffeine_cups, screen_h, stress, skipped_meal, alcohol_units, neck_tension, aura, exercise_min, notes_other. Output JSON only."
sc = tinker.ServiceClient()
tc = sc.create_lora_training_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", rank=32)
tok = tc.get_tokenizer()

def datum(note, row):
    prompt = tok.apply_chat_template([{"role":"system","content":SYSTEM},{"role":"user","content":note}],
                                     add_generation_prompt=True)          # verify: renderer for Qwen3.5 (disable thinking)
    completion = tok.encode(json.dumps(row) + tok.eos_token, add_special_tokens=False)
    full = prompt + completion
    return tinker.types.Datum(
        model_input=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(full[:-1]),         # verify field name: input vs model_input
        loss_fn_inputs={"target_tokens": full[1:],
                        "weights": [0.0]*(len(prompt)-1) + [1.0]*len(completion)})

data = [json.loads(l) for l in open("data/train.jsonl")]
for epoch in range(3):
    random.shuffle(data)
    for i in range(0, len(data), 16):
        batch = [datum(d["note"], d["row"]) for d in data[i:i+16]]
        fb = tc.forward_backward(batch, loss_fn="cross_entropy")
        tc.optim_step(tinker.types.AdamParams(learning_rate=2e-4)).result()
        print(epoch, i, fb.result().metrics)                               # log loss for the post's curve
path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name="heads-up-v1").result().path        # verify; -> tinker://... sampler path
print(path)
```

from tabpfn import TabPFNClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import RepeatedStratifiedKFold, cross_val_score

def train_eval(hist: pd.DataFrame):
    X, y = hist.drop(columns=["date","migraine_next_day"]), hist["migraine_next_day"]
    cv = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=5, random_state=0)
    auc = cross_val_score(TabPFNClassifier(), X, y, cv=cv, scoring="roc_auc")
    return auc.mean(), auc.std()

Yes, your brother counts. The rules say "a friend or someone you love," and family entries are common in this field (the top entry is for a husband).

**Why you need a real person at all:**
1. **It's in the rules.** The entry has to "solve a real problem for a friend or loved one." A made-up person risks disqualification and reads as fake.
2. **Writing quality is weighted most.** The strongest posts in the field all hinge on a named person and what they actually said. "Bonus points if you actually hand it over and tell us what they said" is written into the prompt.
3. **The tech needs his data.** Tinker needs examples of how he actually writes, so the fine-tune beats the base model on his real notes. TabPFN needs his history to forecast from. Without real data, those two $200 categories are just a demo on fake numbers.

**One catch: the project has to fit his real problem.** If your brother doesn't get migraines, don't build a migraine app. Pick something he actually deals with and keep the same stack: his messy notes go in, a fine-tuned model turns them into rows, and TabPFN forecasts something about tomorrow. Some examples:
- **Gym or sport:** "chest day, bench felt heavy, slept 6h" → will he hit a personal best or get sore tomorrow?
- **Studies or exams:** daily study notes → which topics he's likely to fail on the next test
- **Sleep, skin breakouts, allergies or stomach issues:** daily log → chance of a bad day tomorrow
- **Money:** spending texts → will he run out before the end of the month?

**What you need from him (about 15 minutes, before he sleeps):**
- 20 or more examples of how he'd describe his day, in his own words and slang
- His past 1–3 months of history, from his phone notes, chats, gym app or calendar, plus which days the bad thing happened
- Permission to mention him (first name or a nickname) in the post
- Tomorrow morning: 5 minutes trying it, and one honest quote

**What does your brother actually struggle with?** Tell me and I'll rework the idea and the playbook around it, then start building.

# Actually: Playbook (ADHD / time-blindness edition)

> **Supersedes the *domain* parts of `03-PLAYBOOK-heads-up.md`** (data, schema, eval, post). Infrastructure is unchanged and still lives there: bootstrap §H0, Tinker SFT skeleton §2.3, GGUF export + DigitalOcean §H4:30, Sentry §H5:30, Entire, submission checklist Part VI. The stack is the same five: **Tinker · TabPFN · DigitalOcean · Sentry · Entire**.
> **Deadline: Mon Oct 5, 11:59 AM PKT (06:59 UTC). Publish by 10:30 AM PKT.**

## 1. The idea in one breath
Your friend has ADHD. One of the most-reported ADHD struggles is **time blindness**: "this'll take 15 minutes" becomes an hour, the day is over-packed by 9 AM, and the guilt follows. **Actually** takes his messy brain-dump (*"email prof abt extension, laundry maybe, gym, finish dbms assignment, call ammi back"*). A **Tinker-fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B** splits it into structured tasks. Then **TabPFN**, reading *his own* history of guessed vs real durations, tells him **how long each task will actually take *him***, with a range and a reason, and what really fits in the hours he has.

> *"You think this list is 2h10m. For you, it's about 4h40m (3h50–5h30). You've got 3 free hours. Do these three; the laundry and the email can move to tomorrow — you finish admin tasks after 9 PM only 20% of the time."*

**Why this wins:**
- **Not taken.** 8 ADHD/overwhelm entries exist, all with ≤3♥, and all of them are "LLM breaks your task into steps" chat apps (Unstick, Kaizen, BiteSize, Promise Keeper…). **0 of 786 entries tackle time blindness or duration prediction.**
- **TabPFN is the textbook fit, and it gives the most intuitive metric in the contest:** *"TabPFN's estimates of how long his tasks take are [X]% closer to reality than his own guesses."* Every reader, ADHD or not, gets it in one line. It's in-context too: every task he logs makes the next prediction better instantly, with no retraining (a genuine TabPFN-only property worth stating).
- **Tinker has a hard, real job.** Rambling multi-task brain-dumps ("maybe", "after that", Urdu/English mix, slang) are where small base models drop or merge tasks. Measure task-level F1 on *his real* dumps.
- **Open-innovation story is strong.** An ADHD diagnosis, meds, and daily struggles are health data. Everything runs on one Droplet you control, and Sentry traces exclude prompts.

## 2. What to get from your friend TONIGHT (15–20 min; send this message now)

> "Building you something for the hackathon, need 15 min of your help before you sleep:
> 1. Paste me 5–10 brain-dumps / to-do rants you've actually written or sent me (notes app, WhatsApp, anything). Plus write 3 fresh ones right now about tomorrow.
> 2. Fill this sheet with as many tasks as you can remember from the last 2–3 weeks (aim for 40+): what it was, how long you THOUGHT it would take, how long it ACTUALLY took (rough is fine), did it get done the day you planned (y/n), what time you started.
> 3. Is it ok if I write about you in a public post (first name or nickname)?
> 4. Tomorrow morning: try it for 5 minutes and tell me honestly what's wrong with it."

**Sheet columns** (Google Sheet → CSV): `date, task, kind, guess_min, actual_min, done_same_day, start_hour, dreaded(y/n), left_house(y/n)` + optional `slept_h, meds_taken(y/n)`. Kind = admin · study · creative · chore · errand · social · work.

Sources that jog memory: WhatsApp chats with you ("bro still haven't done X"), Google Calendar, uni portal submission timestamps vs deadlines, phone screen-time.
**Honest caveat for the post:** remembered durations are noisy. Say so, then add a small set of *live* logged rows from tomorrow morning if possible.

## 3. Schemas (fix now, never change)

**Tinker parser output** (brain-dump → tasks):
```json
{"tasks": [
  {"title": "email prof about extension", "kind": "admin", "guess_min": null,
   "deadline": "today", "must_leave_house": false, "dreaded": true, "depends_on": null},
  {"title": "laundry", "kind": "chore", "guess_min": 30, "deadline": null,
   "must_leave_house": false, "dreaded": false, "depends_on": null, "optional": true}
]}
```

**TabPFN table** (one row per past task): features `kind, guess_min, start_hour, day_of_week, dreaded, left_house, deadline_hours, [slept_h], [meds_taken]` → targets
- `actual_min`: **TabPFNRegressor** with its predictive distribution → median + 10–90% range ([Predictive Distribution](https://docs.priorlabs.ai/capabilities/predictive-distribution.md))
- `done_same_day`: **TabPFNClassifier** → P(finished today)
- Shapley drivers via `tabpfn-extensions[interpretability]` → "because: admin + after 9 PM + dreaded"

## 4. Eval (these numbers ARE the post)

**TabPFN (the headline):** cross-validated on his rows (repeated 5-fold).

| Estimator of actual duration | MAE (min) | within ±25% |
|---|---|---|
| His own guess | [ ] | [ ]% |
| "Multiply by 2" rule of thumb | [ ] | [ ]% |
| His guess × his median overrun ratio | [ ] | [ ]% |
| Linear regression | [ ] | [ ]% |
| **TabPFN** | **[ ]** | **[ ]%** |

Including the two "dumb" baselines is what makes the result credible. If TabPFN only narrowly beats "his ratio", say so. That is still a finding.

**Tinker:** parser on **his real brain-dumps, hand-labelled** (10–15 dumps ≈ 60–100 tasks).

| Parser | valid JSON | task F1 (found the right tasks) | kind acc | guess_min acc | p50 latency on Droplet |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-4B zero-shot | | | | | |
| Qwen3.5-4B 5-shot | | | | | |
| Qwen3.5-9B zero-shot | | | | | |
| **Qwen3.5-4B + LoRA** | | | | | |

Plus the downstream column: **error in the total-day forecast** when the plan is built from each parser's output. Dropped or merged tasks make the day look shorter than it is, which is exactly the time-blindness bug the app exists to fix. That's a great line for the post.

**Training data:** about 400 synthetic brain-dumps written by a large open teacher on Tinker (e.g. `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B`), seeded with the *style* of 5 of his real dumps (keep the rest as the test set), labelled by the teacher, and spot-checked by you. Cost is under $1.

## 5. Hour plan (PKT, starting ~00:15)

| PKT | Do |
|---|---|
| 00:15–00:45 | Send the friend message. Bootstrap the repo + `entire enable -y --agent claude-code`. Claim Tinker credits. Go/no-go gates (Tinker auth, local `tabpfn` weights, `doctl`). |
| 00:45–02:15 | Synthetic dataset → **start the Tinker SFT run** (it trains while you build). Meanwhile: TabPFN module on his sheet + CV eval table. |
| 02:15–04:00 | FastAPI + one-page UI (frontend-design): brain-dump box → task cards with "you: 15m · actually: 45m (30–70)" → "fits in your free time" plan → one-tap "done + how long". |
| 04:00–05:00 | Parser eval (base vs tuned) → fill table. Export adapter → GGUF → Ollama. |
| 05:00–06:00 | DigitalOcean Droplet up, HTTPS via sslip.io, demo profile with synthetic data, private profile with a passphrase. |
| 06:00–06:30 | Sentry traces (base vs tuned latency, one bug found) → screenshots. |
| **06:30–08:00** | **Sleep 90 min** (an alarm-proof one). |
| 08:00–08:30 | Friend tries it. Get their verbatim reaction, make one fix. |
| 08:30–10:15 | Write the post (structure §6), cover image, 60–90 s video. |
| **10:15–10:30** | Checklist (Part VI of heads-up playbook) → **PUBLISH**. Then MLH Discord + socials. |
| 11:59 | Deadline. |

**Cut order if behind:** (1) Sentry → (2) GGUF self-hosting (use the Tinker OpenAI endpoint; DO still hosts the app) → (3) the downstream parser column. **Never cut:** the TabPFN-vs-his-guesses table, the friend's quote, the live link.

## 6. Post outline (template headings, exact)

Title candidates:
1. *"My friend thinks everything takes 15 minutes. I built him a model that knows better."*
2. *"Time blindness, measured: TabPFN guesses my ADHD friend's tasks [X]% better than he does"*

- **Opening:** "[Friend] has ADHD. Ask him how long an email takes and he'll say five minutes. Last [Tuesday] it took [real story]." + the honest "I can't fix time blindness, but I can show him the number."
- **What I Built:** brain-dump in → real durations + a day that actually fits. Screenshot.
- **Demo:** live link (demo profile) + video.
- **Code:** repo embed, MIT, `eval/` reproduces every number.
- **How I Built It:** (1) Tinker parser + table; (2) TabPFN + the his-guess-vs-TabPFN table + Shapley "why"; (3) one DigitalOcean Droplet; (4) Sentry traces + the bug; capability grid with honest ✗s.
- **Why Does Open Innovation Matter?:** health data on his box; a model fine-tuned to *his* ramble that you can't get from a closed API; runs for ~nothing and outlives the hackathon. Plus one line where closed would have been better.
- **What [Friend] said:** verbatim quote + "He said / What I changed" table.
- **My Agent Session:** Entire checkpoint links (3–4 key decisions) (+ optional DevRelay).
- **Prize Categories:** Tinker · TabPFN · DigitalOcean · Sentry Agent Tracing · Entire, one line of proof each.
- **Closing question:** "If you have ADHD: what's the task you're *always* wrong about?"

**Sensitivity rule:** describe ADHD the way your friend describes it, and let him read the post before you publish. No medical claims. It's "a planning aid", not treatment.

entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to [REDACTED_EMAIL]' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
entries.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__list_connected_browsers
entries.description: List all Chrome browsers (extension instances) currently connected to this account. Returns each browser's deviceId, display name, OS platform, isLocal (its OS matches this computer's, a weak hint), when known onThisComputer (it is, or recently was, running on this computer), and inUse on the browser this session's actions go to when that is settled. When the user needs to choose a browser, use this to present the choices before select_browser. You do not need to call this before using the browser: when one browser is connected, or one was already chosen for this session, browser tools just work. Only if a browser tool reports that several browsers are connected and none is selected, or the user asks to change browsers, ask with the AskUserQuestion tool: one option per connected browser, the ones on this computer first (display name as the label, deviceId in parentheses), plus a final option labeled exactly: "Open a confirmation screen in every connected Chrome extension and let me select the right one there." Then call select_browser with the chosen deviceId, or switch_browser for the final option. Never pick one yourself.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp

The project is started. The repo is `~/theodinproject/repos/actually`, Entire is recording sessions there, the first commit is made, and Python packages are installing in the background. Here's everything I need from you.

## 1. Reconnect the browser (blocking)
The Claude Chrome extension isn't connected. Open Chrome and check the extension is installed and signed into claude.ai with the same account as this terminal. Restart Chrome if needed, then tell me and I'll drive.

## 2. Accounts: I drive, you handle logins, 2FA, CAPTCHAs and any card entry
I won't type passwords or card numbers. I'll navigate, create keys, and save them to `.env`, which never gets committed.

| # | Site | You do | I do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | hacktoberfest.com/my/promos | Log in | Read the Tinker code, and a DigitalOcean one if offered |
| 2 | tinker.thinkingmachines.ai | Log in, redeem credit | Create API key |
| 3 | DigitalOcean | Log in; add a card if there are no credits | Create API token, then the server |
| 4 | platform.priorlabs.ai, and Hugging Face if it asks | Log in | Create key, accept the TabPFN model license (needed to download the model) |
| 5 | sentry.io (free) | Log in or sign up | Create project, copy the key |
| 6 | Entire | Approve one browser login prompt | Run `entire login` |

## 3. Your friend's data (before you sleep)
Put these two files in `~/theodinproject/repos/actually/data/private/`:
- `brain_dumps.txt`: 8–15 real to-do rants, separated by `---`
- `tasks.csv` with these columns:
  `date,task,kind,guess_min,actual_min,done_same_day,start_hour,dreaded,left_house`

  Aim for 40+ rows. Rough numbers are fine.

If it doesn't arrive tonight, I'll build and test on clearly labelled synthetic data, then rerun everything on his data in the morning. **Every number in the post must come from his data.**

## 4. Yes/no approvals
1. Push a public GitHub repo `ArqamWaheed/actually`? The submission requires public code, and his data is never included.
2. Spend up to about **$25**: one DigitalOcean server with 8 CPUs and 16 GB RAM, about $0.14 an hour, deleted after judging, plus any Tinker cost beyond the credits.
3. Clear the npm and uv download caches, about 2 GB? Your home disk has only **2.6 GB free**. Everything in them can be re-downloaded.
4. What name or nickname should the post use for your friend?

## 5. What I won't do overnight
- Publish the DEV post. It needs his reaction, and it goes out under your name. I'll leave a finished draft with gaps only for his quote.
- Enter any payment details.
- Invent data, quotes or results.

"""TabPFN on the friend's own task history.

Regressor: how long a task will actually take him (median + 10-90% range).
Classifier: probability he finishes it the day he planned it.
Both are in-context: every logged task improves the next prediction with no retraining.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as dt
import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

FEATURES = ["kind", "guess_min", "start_hour", "day_of_week", "dreaded", "left_house", "has_deadline"]
MIN_ROWS = 12


def load_history(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = pd.read_csv(path)
    df.columns = [c.strip().lower() for c in df.columns]
    for c in ("dreaded", "left_house", "done_same_day"):
        if c in df:
            df[c] = df[c].astype(str).str.strip().str.lower().isin(["y", "yes", "1", "true"]).astype(int)
    if "date" in df:
        df["day_of_week"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"], errors="coerce").dt.dayofweek
    df["has_deadline"] = df.get("has_deadline", 0)
    df = df[pd.to_numeric(df["actual_min"], errors="coerce").notna()].copy()
    df["actual_min"] = df["actual_min"].astype(float)
    df["guess_min"] = pd.to_numeric(df["guess_min"], errors="coerce")
    return df


def task_rows(tasks, now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    now = now or dt.datetime.now()
    return pd.DataFrame([{
        "kind": t.kind,
        "guess_min": t.guess_min if t.guess_min is not None else np.nan,
        "start_hour": now.hour,
        "day_of_week": now.weekday(),
        "dreaded": int(t.dreaded),
        "left_house": int(t.must_leave_house),
        "has_deadline": int(t.deadline is not None),
    } for t in tasks])


class Forecaster:
    def __init__(self, history: pd.DataFrame):
        from tabpfn import TabPFNClassifier, TabPFNRegressor

        self.history = history
        X = history[FEATURES]
        # log-duration: durations are right-skewed; TabPFN is happier on the log scale
        self.reg = TabPFNRegressor().fit(X, np.log1p(history["actual_min"]))
        self.clf = None
        y = history.get("done_same_day")
        if y is not None and y.nunique() == 2:
            self.clf = TabPFNClassifier().fit(X, y)
        self.overrun = float(np.nanmedian(history["actual_min"] / history["guess_min"]))

    def predict(self, rows: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
        q = self.reg.predict(rows[FEATURES], output_type="quantiles", quantiles=[0.1, 0.5, 0.9])
        p10, p50, p90 = (np.expm1(np.asarray(a)) for a in q)
        p_done = self.clf.predict_proba(rows[FEATURES])[:, 1] if self.clf is not None else [None] * len(rows)
        return {"p10": p10, "p50": p50, "p90": p90, "p_done": p_done}

    def why(self, row: pd.Series) -> list[str]:
        """Plain-English drivers from the friend's own history (cheap, deterministic).
        Shapley attributions (tabpfn-extensions) are computed offline in eval/ for the post."""
        h, out = self.history, []
        same = h[h["kind"] == row["kind"]]
        if len(same) >= 3 and same["guess_min"].notna().any():
            r = float(np.nanmedian(same["actual_min"] / same["guess_min"]))
            if math.isfinite(r) and r > 1.2:
                out.append(f"{row['kind']} tasks take you ~{r:.1f}x your guess")
        if row["dreaded"] and h["dreaded"].sum() >= 3:
            d = h.groupby("dreaded")["actual_min"].median()
            if 1 in d and 0 in d and d[1] > d[0]:
                out.append(f"dreaded tasks run ~{d[1] / d[0]:.1f}x longer for you")
        late = h[h["start_hour"] >= 21]
        if row["start_hour"] >= 21 and len(late) >= 3 and "done_same_day" in h:
            out.append(f"you finish only {late['done_same_day'].mean():.0%} of tasks started after 9 PM")
        return out[:3]

"""SQLite on the host box: logged tasks become new TabPFN context rows."""
import os
import sqlite3

DB_PATH = os.getenv("DB_PATH", "actually.db")


def conn():
    c = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    c.execute("""CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS logged (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, profile TEXT, date TEXT, task TEXT, kind TEXT, guess_min REAL,
        actual_min REAL, done_same_day INTEGER, start_hour INTEGER, dreaded INTEGER, left_house INTEGER,
        has_deadline INTEGER)""")
    return c


def log_task(profile: str, row: dict):
    with conn() as c:
        c.execute("""INSERT INTO logged (profile,date,task,kind,guess_min,actual_min,done_same_day,start_hour,
                     dreaded,left_house,has_deadline) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""",
                  (profile, row["date"], row["task"], row["kind"], row.get("guess_min"), row["actual_min"],
                   row.get("done_same_day", 1), row["start_hour"], row.get("dreaded", 0),
                   row.get("left_house", 0), row.get("has_deadline", 0)))


def logged_rows(profile: str):
    import pandas as pd

    with conn() as c:
        return pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM logged WHERE profile = ?", c, params=(profile,))

"""Sentry Agent Tracing. Prompts are never sent: the friend's brain-dumps stay on the box."""
import contextlib
import os

import sentry_sdk


def init():
    dsn = os.getenv("SENTRY_DSN")
    if not dsn:
        return
    from sentry_sdk.integrations.openai import OpenAIIntegration

    sentry_sdk.init(
        dsn=dsn,
        traces_sample_rate=1.0,
        send_default_pii=False,
        integrations=[OpenAIIntegration(include_prompts=False)],
        environment=os.getenv("APP_ENV", "dev"),
    )


@contextlib.contextmanager
def agent_span(name: str = "actually"):
    with sentry_sdk.start_span(op="gen_ai.invoke_agent", name=f"invoke_agent {name}") as span:
        span.set_data("gen_ai.operation.name", "invoke_agent")
        span.set_data("gen_ai.agent.name", name)
        yield span


@contextlib.contextmanager
def tool_span(tool: str):
    with sentry_sdk.start_span(op="gen_ai.execute_tool", name=f"execute_tool {tool}") as span:
        span.set_data("gen_ai.operation.name", "execute_tool")
        span.set_data("gen_ai.tool.name", tool)
        yield span

"""SQLite on the host box: logged tasks become new TabPFN context rows."""
import os
import sqlite3

def conn():
    c = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)

        has_deadline INTEGER)""")

"""SYNTHETIC demo profile for the public live demo. Not the friend's data, and labelled as such in the UI.

Generative story (so TabPFN has real structure to find): admin/dreaded/late-night tasks overrun more.
"""
import csv
import datetime as dt
import random
from pathlib import Path

random.seed(7)
TASKS = {
    "admin": ["email prof about extension", "fill scholarship form", "reply to landlord", "pay internet bill",
              "book dentist", "renew cnic appointment"],
    "study": ["dbms assignment", "revise os chapter 4", "finish lab report", "watch lecture 7", "past paper q3"],
    "chore": ["laundry", "clean room", "dishes", "fold clothes"],
    "errand": ["groceries", "pick up parcel", "print notes"],
    "social": ["call ammi back", "reply to group chat", "birthday msg for hamza"],
    "creative": ["edit reel", "sketch logo idea"],
    "work": ["update resume", "fix freelance bug"],
    "health": ["gym", "go for a walk"],
}
BASE = {"admin": 15, "study": 60, "chore": 30, "errand": 40, "social": 15, "creative": 45, "work": 50, "health": 50}
OVERRUN = {"admin": 2.6, "study": 1.7, "chore": 1.3, "errand": 1.5, "social": 1.8, "creative": 2.0, "work": 1.9,
           "health": 1.2}

out = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data/demo/tasks_demo.csv"
out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
start = dt.date(2026, 9, 10)
with out.open("w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["date", "task", "kind", "guess_min", "actual_min", "done_same_day", "start_hour", "dreaded",
                "left_house"])
    for i in range(70):
        kind = random.choice(list(TASKS))
        day = start + dt.timedelta(days=i // 3)
        hour = random.choice([10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 23])
        dreaded = kind in ("admin", "study") and random.random() < 0.6
        left = kind in ("errand", "health")
        guess = int(BASE[kind] * random.uniform(0.6, 1.2) / 5) * 5 or 5
        mult = OVERRUN[kind] * (1.5 if dreaded else 1) * (1.3 if hour >= 21 else 1) * random.lognormvariate(0, 0.25)
        actual = max(5, round(guess * mult))
        done = int(random.random() > (0.25 + 0.3 * dreaded + 0.25 * (hour >= 21)))
        w.writerow([day.isoformat(), random.choice(TASKS[kind]), kind, guess, actual, "y" if done else "n", hour,
                    "y" if dreaded else "n", "y" if left else "n"])
print("wrote", out)

"""Synthetic training data for the parser, made by a large OPEN teacher model on Tinker.

1. The teacher writes brain-dumps in the friend's style (style seeds = a few of his real dumps,
   never the held-out test dumps).
2. The teacher labels each dump with the exact schema in app/prompts.py.
Output: data/synthetic/train.jsonl  ({"note": str, "gold": {"tasks": [...]}})

Usage: python -m train.gen_synthetic --n 400 --seeds data/private/style_seeds.txt
"""
import argparse
import json
import random
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import tinker
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from app.parser import TinkerParser, render_prompt

load_dotenv()
TEACHER = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B"

SCENARIOS = [
    "a uni student the night before a deadline", "a lazy sunday with chores piling up",
    "a monday with classes, gym and family calls", "a day full of admin they keep avoiding",
    "a freelance + study day", "exam week panic", "after a bad night's sleep", "a day with errands across town",
    "a weekend with a wedding to attend", "a guilt-heavy day after skipping yesterday's plans",
]
WRITE_PROMPT = """Write ONE realistic, messy brain-dump (a to-do rant) by a young person in Pakistan with ADHD, for: {scenario}.
Style rules: write like these real examples (casual, run-on, lowercase, some Urdu/English mix, "maybe", "ugh", tangents):
{seeds}
Mention {k} distinct tasks. Sometimes state a duration ("should take 20 min"), sometimes not. Output only the brain-dump text."""


def write_dump(sampler, tok, seeds: list[str]) -> str:
    seed_txt = "\n---\n".join(random.sample(seeds, min(3, len(seeds))))
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": WRITE_PROMPT.format(scenario=random.choice(SCENARIOS), seeds=seed_txt,
                                                           k=random.randint(2, 8))}]
    res = sampler.sample(prompt=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(render_prompt(tok, msgs)), num_samples=1,
                         sampling_params=tinker.types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=400, temperature=0.9)).result()
    return tok.decode(res.sequences[0].tokens, skip_special_tokens=True).strip()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=400)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="data/private/style_seeds.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/synthetic/train.jsonl")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    seeds = [s.strip() for s in Path(a.seeds).read_text().split("---") if s.strip()]
    sampler = tinker.ServiceClient().create_sampling_client(base_model=TEACHER)
    tok = sampler.get_tokenizer()
    labeler = TinkerParser(TEACHER)

    def one(_):
        dump = write_dump(sampler, tok, seeds)
        r = labeler.parse(dump)
        return {"note": dump, "gold": r.tasks.model_dump()} if r.tasks and r.tasks.tasks else None

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
        rows = [r for r in ex.map(one, range(a.n)) if r]
    Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(a.out, "w") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(rows)}/{a.n} -> {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-4B on Tinker. Loss only on the assistant JSON tokens.

Usage: python -m train.sft --data data/synthetic/train.jsonl --epochs 3
Prints the sampler path (tinker://...) to put in .env as TINKER_SAMPLER_PATH.
"""
import argparse
import json
import random

import tinker
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from app.parser import messages, render_prompt

load_dotenv()
BASE = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"


def make_datum(tok, note: str, gold: dict) -> tinker.types.Datum:
    prompt = render_prompt(tok, messages(note))
    completion = tok.encode(json.dumps(gold, ensure_ascii=False) + "<|im_end|>", add_special_tokens=False)
    full = prompt + completion
    weights = [0.0] * (len(prompt) - 1) + [1.0] * len(completion)
    return tinker.types.Datum(
        model_input=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(full[:-1]),
        loss_fn_inputs={"target_tokens": full[1:], "weights": weights},
    )


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--data", default="data/synthetic/train.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="actually-v1")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(a.data)]
    tc = tinker.ServiceClient().create_lora_training_client(base_model=BASE, rank=a.rank)
    tok = tc.get_tokenizer()
    data = [make_datum(tok, r["note"], r["gold"]) for r in rows]
    steps = a.epochs * ((len(data) + a.batch - 1) // a.batch)
    step, log = 0, open("results/train_log.jsonl", "w")
    for epoch in range(a.epochs):
        random.shuffle(data)
        for i in range(0, len(data), a.batch):
            lr = a.lr * (1 - step / steps)  # linear decay
            fb = tc.forward_backward(data[i:i + a.batch], loss_fn="cross_entropy")
            tc.optim_step(adam_params=tinker.types.AdamParams(learning_rate=lr)).result()
            out = fb.result()
            metrics = getattr(out, "metrics", {}) or {}
            log.write(json.dumps({"step": step, "epoch": epoch, "lr": lr, **metrics}) + "\n")
            log.flush()
            print(step, epoch, {k: round(v, 4) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in metrics.items()})
            step += 1
    path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name=a.name).result().path
    print("SAMPLER_PATH", path)
    with open("results/sampler_path.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write(path + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

   never the held-out test dumps).
2. The teacher labels each dump with the exact schema in app/prompts.py.
Output: data/synthetic/train.jsonl  ({"note": str, "gold": {"tasks": [...]}})

Usage: python -m train.gen_synthetic --n 400 --seeds data/private/style_seeds.txt
"""
import argparse
import json
import random
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import tinker
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from app.parser import TinkerParser, render_prompt

load_dotenv()
TEACHER = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B"

SCENARIOS = [
    "a uni student the night before a deadline", "a lazy sunday with chores piling up",
    "a monday with classes, gym and family calls", "a day full of admin they keep avoiding",
    "a freelance + study day", "exam week panic", "after a bad night's sleep", "a day with errands across town",
    "a weekend with a wedding to attend", "a guilt-heavy day after skipping yesterday's plans",
]
WRITE_PROMPT = """Write ONE realistic, messy brain-dump (a to-do rant) by a young person in Pakistan with ADHD, for: {scenario}.
Style rules: write like these real examples (casual, run-on, lowercase, some Urdu/English mix, "maybe", "ugh", tangents):
{seeds}
Mention {k} distinct tasks. Sometimes state a duration ("should take 20 min"), sometimes not. Output only the brain-dump text."""


def write_dump(sampler, tok, seeds: list[str]) -> str:
    seed_txt = "\n---\n".join(random.sample(seeds, min(3, len(seeds))))
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": WRITE_PROMPT.format(scenario=random.choice(SCENARIOS), seeds=seed_txt,
                                                           k=random.randint(2, 8))}]
    res = sampler.sample(prompt=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(render_prompt(tok, msgs)), num_samples=1,
                         sampling_params=tinker.types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=400, temperature=0.9)).result()
    return tok.decode(res.sequences[0].tokens, skip_special_tokens=True).strip()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=400)
    ap.add_argument("--seeds", default="data/private/style_seeds.txt")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="data/synthetic/train.jsonl")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    seeds = [s.strip() for s in Path(a.seeds).read_text().split("---") if s.strip()]
    sampler = tinker.ServiceClient().create_sampling_client(base_model=TEACHER)
    tok = sampler.get_tokenizer()
    labeler = TinkerParser(TEACHER)

    def one(_):
        dump = write_dump(sampler, tok, seeds)
        r = labeler.parse(dump)
        return {"note": dump, "gold": r.tasks.model_dump()} if r.tasks and r.tasks.tasks else None

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
        rows = [r for r in ex.map(one, range(a.n)) if r]
    Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(a.out, "w") as f:
        for r in rows:
            f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"wrote {len(rows)}/{a.n} -> {a.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""LoRA SFT of Qwen3.5-4B on Tinker. Loss only on the assistant JSON tokens.

Usage: python -m train.sft --data data/synthetic/train.jsonl --epochs 3
Prints the sampler path (tinker://...) to put in .env as TINKER_SAMPLER_PATH.
"""
import argparse
import json
import random

import tinker
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from app.parser import messages, render_prompt

load_dotenv()
BASE = "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"


def make_datum(tok, note: str, gold: dict) -> tinker.types.Datum:
    prompt = render_prompt(tok, messages(note))
    completion = tok.encode(json.dumps(gold, ensure_ascii=False) + "<|im_end|>", add_special_tokens=False)
    full = prompt + completion
    weights = [0.0] * (len(prompt) - 1) + [1.0] * len(completion)
    return tinker.types.Datum(
        model_input=tinker.types.ModelInput.from_ints(full[:-1]),
        loss_fn_inputs={"target_tokens": full[1:], "weights": weights},
    )


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--data", default="data/synthetic/train.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--name", default="actually-v1")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(a.data)]
    tc = tinker.ServiceClient().create_lora_training_client(base_model=BASE, rank=a.rank)
    tok = tc.get_tokenizer()
    data = [make_datum(tok, r["note"], r["gold"]) for r in rows]
    steps = a.epochs * ((len(data) + a.batch - 1) // a.batch)
    step, log = 0, open("results/train_log.jsonl", "w")
    for epoch in range(a.epochs):
        random.shuffle(data)
        for i in range(0, len(data), a.batch):
            lr = a.lr * (1 - step / steps)  # linear decay
            fb = tc.forward_backward(data[i:i + a.batch], loss_fn="cross_entropy")
            tc.optim_step(adam_params=tinker.types.AdamParams(learning_rate=lr)).result()
            out = fb.result()
            metrics = getattr(out, "metrics", {}) or {}
            log.write(json.dumps({"step": step, "epoch": epoch, "lr": lr, **metrics}) + "\n")
            log.flush()
            print(step, epoch, {k: round(v, 4) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in metrics.items()})
            step += 1
    path = tc.save_weights_for_sampler(name=a.name).result().path
    print("SAMPLER_PATH", path)
    with open("results/sampler_path.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write(path + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Headline eval: does TabPFN predict how long his tasks take better than he does?

Repeated K-fold CV on the task history. Baselines: his own guess, "x2" rule, his-median-overrun x guess,
linear regression. Usage: python -m eval.tabpfn_eval --csv data/private/tasks.csv --label friend
"""
import argparse
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import RepeatedKFold
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder

from app.forecast import FEATURES, load_history


def metrics(y, p):
    y, p = np.asarray(y), np.asarray(p)
    return {"mae_min": float(np.mean(np.abs(y - p))), "within_25pct": float(np.mean(np.abs(p - y) <= 0.25 * y))}


def main():
    from tabpfn import TabPFNRegressor

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--csv", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--label", default="demo")
    ap.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=3)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    df = load_history(a.csv)
    df = df[df["guess_min"].notna()].reset_index(drop=True)
    X, y = df[FEATURES], df["actual_min"].values
    preds = {k: np.zeros((a.repeats, len(df))) for k in ["his_guess", "x2_rule", "his_overrun", "linear", "tabpfn"]}
    lin = make_pipeline(
        ColumnTransformer([("cat", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore"), ["kind"])], remainder="passthrough"),
        SimpleImputer(), LinearRegression())
    rkf = RepeatedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=a.repeats, random_state=0)
    for j, (tr, te) in enumerate(rkf.split(X)):
        r = j // 5
        g = df.loc[te, "guess_min"].values
        preds["his_guess"][r, te] = g
        preds["x2_rule"][r, te] = 2 * g
        ratio = np.nanmedian(y[tr] / df.loc[tr, "guess_min"].values)
        preds["his_overrun"][r, te] = ratio * g
        preds["linear"][r, te] = np.expm1(lin.fit(X.iloc[tr], np.log1p(y[tr])).predict(X.iloc[te]))
        m = TabPFNRegressor().fit(X.iloc[tr], np.log1p(y[tr]))
        preds["tabpfn"][r, te] = np.expm1(m.predict(X.iloc[te], output_type="median"))
    res = {}
    for k, P in preds.items():
        per = [metrics(y, P[r]) for r in range(a.repeats)]
        res[k] = {m: float(np.mean([p[m] for p in per])) for m in per[0]}
    out = {"label": a.label, "n_tasks": len(df), "results": res}
    print(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
    with open(f"results/tabpfn_eval_{a.label}.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    names = {"his_guess": "His own guess", "x2_rule": '"Double it" rule', "his_overrun": "His guess x his median overrun",
             "linear": "Linear regression", "tabpfn": "**TabPFN**"}
    lines = ["| Estimator | MAE (min) | within ±25% |", "|---|---|---|"]
    lines += [f"| {names[k]} | {v['mae_min']:.1f} | {v['within_25pct']:.0%} |" for k, v in res.items()]
    open(f"results/tabpfn_eval_{a.label}.md", "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    print("\n".join(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
